<!--
  THE AGENT'S JOB DESCRIPTION — editable capability text, same as prompt.md.

  Everything below is sent to the agent as its first user message, so it is part of the
  skill you are optimizing: reword it, restructure it, add or remove guidance, change the
  interaction contract. This comment block is STRIPPED before the agent sees it.

  LOAD-BEARING PLACEHOLDERS — these are filled in per task and must SURVIVE any edit:
    {instruction} {spreadsheet_path} {spreadsheet_content} {instruction_type}
    {answer_position} {output_path}
  Optional: {max_turns}. No other {braces} are allowed.

  If a required placeholder goes missing, or an unknown one appears, the candidate is
  REJECTED before any task runs — the agent would otherwise be told to write its answer to
  a path it was never given. A literal brace must be doubled: {{ or }}.
-->
You need to solve the following spreadsheet manipulation question. It contains six pieces of information:
- instruction: the question about spreadsheet manipulation.
- spreadsheet_path: the path of the spreadsheet file you need to manipulate.
- spreadsheet_content: the target range's total size, the location of the other graded copies
  of this workbook, each sheet's real data extent, and the first few rows of the content.
- instruction_type: Cell-Level Manipulation (answer_position is exact cell(s)) or Sheet-Level Manipulation (answer_position is the maximum range you may modify).
- answer_position: the cell(s)/range you must modify or fill in.
- output_path: write the modified spreadsheet file to this exact path.

### instruction
{instruction}

### spreadsheet_path
{spreadsheet_path}

### spreadsheet_content
{spreadsheet_content}

### instruction_type
{instruction_type}

### answer_position
{answer_position}

### output_path
{output_path}

### how this is graded (read before writing code)
Your FINAL solution code block is re-run UNCHANGED on three copies of this workbook whose
data differs (row counts and values change); each resulting output file is graded. Only the
spreadsheet_content preview above (copy 1) is visible to you. So your code must recompute the
answer from whatever data it finds — it must NOT bake in anything specific to copy 1:
- Do NOT assume a pattern you see in the preview holds on the other copies — e.g. that every
  row has the same status/category, that the data is a fixed number of rows, that a value sits
  in one specific cell, or that a summary/helper table implies a fixed constraint. Detect the
  real data extent at run time (scan to the last non-empty row; find any label/marker/"answer"
  row by its text content, not by a hardcoded row number).
- The answer_position range is the SAME on all three copies — always write your answer there.
- In an EARLY turn, open and inspect ALL THREE input copies (their paths are listed in
  spreadsheet_content), not just copy 1, and confirm your approach produces the right answer on
  each before you finalize. The final block itself must still read only the one spreadsheet_path.
- The re-run swaps in the other copies by literally substituting the input/output filenames in your
  final block, so in it use the exact spreadsheet_path and output_path strings given above verbatim —
  do not glob for files or build paths from the copy number, or copies 2 and 3 will get no output.

Each answer cell is compared by BOTH value AND type: numbers as numbers (rounded to 2 decimals),
text compared exactly, dates as dates. Write each answer in the same TYPE the expected result
uses. When you split or extract text, keep each extracted piece as text — do NOT convert a text
fragment into a datetime or a number unless the instruction asks you to compute one. Blank, None,
and empty string all count as empty; leave a cell empty rather than writing a 0 placeholder where
the answer is blank.

Fill only the cells the instruction actually asks for. Do NOT add extra labels, totals, headers,
or summary rows it didn't request, and do NOT change values the task doesn't require — for
formatting or conditional-formatting tasks, keep the existing cell values and formulas unchanged
and modify only the formatting. Take the simplest reading of the instruction that fits the data;
once your output satisfies the instruction, do not replace it with a more elaborate computation
during verification unless you find a concrete error.

You have up to {max_turns} rounds of interaction. In each round, reply with exactly ONE python code block:
1. Information-gathering code (e.g. inspecting all three input copies) — the result is returned to you.
2. Solution code that writes the modified file to output_path.
3. Verification code: re-open output_path and print the value AND the python type of each cell in
   answer_position. Confirm every required cell holds the intended value in the intended type (e.g.
   a text answer is a str, a numeric answer is a number, a date is a date) — an unintended None or a
   type mismatch means the grader will reject it. If anything is wrong, fix your code and write again.
Reply without a code block when you are satisfied the saved file is correct.
If your code raises an error, the traceback will be returned to you; fix the code and try again.
